extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in research integrity (researchers, editors, librarians, publishers, and watchdogs)
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and evaluate signs of compromised editorial handling, peer review manipulation, and other integrity problems in journal articles and special/guest-edited issues, and consider publisher responses and remediation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compromised editorial handling and peer review process
rubrics_metrics.description: An investigation by the publisher found a number of articles with concerns including compromised editorial handling and peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such compromise is a core reason for loss of confidence in results and conclusions and is explicitly cited in retraction notices; flag patterns suggesting manipulated reviewer selection, fake reviews, or inadequate oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate or irrelevant references
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles contain inappropriate or irrelevant references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of irrelevant or inappropriate citations can indicate low quality, citation manipulation, or attempts to game metrics; it is one of the listed concerns prompting retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article out of scope for the journal or guest-edited issue
rubrics_metrics.description: The article is not in scope of the journal or the guest-edited issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope mismatch—especially within guest-edited issues—serves as a red flag for poor editorial vetting and is cited among reasons for retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing retracted or otherwise problematic papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles that cite retracted or otherwise problematic papers (flagged by tools such as the Problematic Paper Screener).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High numbers of articles citing retracted/problematic work indicate systemic issues with quality control; reviewers/editors should check references for retractions or dubious sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'tortured phrases' and nonstandard language
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of 'tortured phrases'—nonstandard language that hints at use of a thesaurus or paraphrasing software to avoid plagiarism detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such language patterns are indicators of paper manipulation or automated rewriting; screening tools and manual checks can identify these signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concerns associated with guest-edited issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple problematic articles concentrated in guest-edited issues, with content retracted from at least 10 guest-edited issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guest-edited issues can be vulnerable to exploitation; evaluate guest-editor selection, oversight, and the special-issue proposal process when assessing integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher investigation leading to retraction when lacking confidence in results
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher states that 'based on the investigation’s findings the publisher no longer has confidence in the results and conclusions of this article.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loss of confidence (due to any combination of editorial/peer-review compromise, scope mismatch, inappropriate references, etc.) is the formal trigger for retraction; documentation of the investigation and its findings is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual assessment of articles rather than blanket issue retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher assesses each article individually rather than retracting entire issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy of article-by-article assessment aims to avoid collateral retractions but requires robust, transparent case-by-case investigations and clear retraction notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight and governance reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher actions include updating the editorial board, ensuring the editor-in-chief oversees every paper, no longer considering unsolicited proposals for special issues, and adding new research integrity tools to the submission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are recommended or implemented mitigation measures: strengthen oversight, centralize final decision-making, restrict special-issue workflows, and deploy integrity screening tools at submission to reduce future problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of whistleblower information and proactive screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Retractions and investigations are informed by publisher investigations and whistleblower information; sleuths using screening tools have also flagged problematic articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine internal investigations, whistleblower reports, and automated screening (e.g., problematic-paper screeners) to detect patterns of manipulation or poor quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized retraction notice language
rubrics_metrics.description: Retraction notes contain identical language across multiple journals, listing concerns 'including but not limited to compromised editorial handling and peer review process, inappropriate or irrelevant references or not being in scope of the journal or guest-edited issue.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent retraction wording can communicate the categories of concern while remaining somewhat generic; evaluators should seek the underlying investigation details when available.
